lessons.title: Asset Quality: GNPA, NNPA, Provision Coverage, and Credit Cost

body.text: A bank earns its margin slowly, one quarter at a time, and can lose years of it in a single bad lending cycle. NIM tells you how much a bank earns. Asset quality tells you how much of that it gets to keep. For bank stocks, bad loans are not one risk among many; they are the risk.

children.text: Think about the leverage from Chapter 1. A bank with 10 times leverage has roughly ₹10 of loans for every ₹1 of its own equity. If just 5% of those loans are never repaid and nothing has been set aside, half the equity is gone. That is why the market can forgive a bank a slow quarter of loan growth but punishes a surprise in bad loans immediately. This lesson teaches you the four numbers that measure asset quality and how to read them together.

markDefs.definition: Special Mention Account: the RBI's early warning buckets for loans that are overdue but not yet classified as NPAs, split by how many days payments are overdue.

children.text: Under RBI norms, a term loan becomes a Non-Performing Asset (NPA) when interest or principal remains overdue for more than 90 days. Before that point, lenders track stress through
categories. Once a loan is an NPA, it ages through further categories, and the longer it stays bad, the more the bank must provide for it.

body.caption: The Journey From Late Payment to Loss

cells: Early sign of stress, often just a delayed payment
Next stop is NPA; the most useful leading indicator

body.latex: \text{GNPA \%} = \frac{\text{Gross NPAs}}{\text{Gross advances}} \qquad \text{NNPA \%} = \frac{\text{Gross NPAs} - \text{Provisions}}{\text{Gross advances} - \text{Provisions}} \qquad \text{PCR} = \frac{\text{Provisions on NPAs}}{\text{Gross NPAs}} \qquad \text{Credit cost} = \frac{\text{Loan loss provisions for the year}}{\text{Average advances}}
body.caption: Gross NPA ratio, Net NPA ratio, Provision Coverage Ratio, and credit cost

children.text: Each number answers a different question. GNPA tells you how much of the loan book has gone bad. NNPA tells you how much of that bad debt is still not covered by provisions, which is the part that can still hurt future profits. PCR tells you how conservatively the bank has already absorbed the damage. Credit cost tells you how much this year's profit was reduced by provisioning, and is the number that links asset quality directly to earnings.

body.title: Calculate Bank M's Net NPA Ratio
body.prompt: Bank M has gross advances of ₹1,00,000 crore, gross NPAs of ₹3,000 crore, and provisions of ₹2,100 crore. What is its Net NPA ratio? Round to two decimal places.
body.explanation: Net NPAs = ₹3,000 crore - ₹2,100 crore = ₹900 crore. Net advances = ₹1,00,000 crore - ₹2,100 crore = ₹97,900 crore. NNPA = 900 ÷ 97,900 = 0.92%. For Bank N: (3,000 - 1,200) ÷ (1,00,000 - 1,200) = 1,800 ÷ 98,800 = 1.82%. Identical GNPA, but Bank N's NNPA is roughly double.

children.text: GNPA Is a Stock; Slippages Are the Flow

The GNPA ratio is a snapshot at a point in time. What actually changes it is movement: new loans turning bad, called slippages, and bad loans leaving the pool through recoveries, upgrades back to standard, or write-offs. Most banks disclose this movement in their investor presentation. Always look at it, because a GNPA ratio can fall for good reasons or for cosmetic ones.

cells: Decreases (loan removed from books, not recovered)

body.title: Roll Forward the NPA Book
body.prompt: Using the table above, what are the bank's closing gross NPAs, in ₹ crore?
body.explanation: Closing GNPA = 4,000 + 1,800 - 700 - 400 - 1,200 = ₹3,500 crore. GNPA fell by ₹500 crore, which looks like improvement. But write-offs of ₹1,200 crore did more to reduce it than recoveries and upgrades combined (₹1,100 crore), and fresh slippages of ₹1,800 crore were substantial. If the opening loan book was ₹1,00,000 crore, the slippage ratio is 1,800 ÷ 1,00,000 = 1.8%. Watch that number over time.

body.text: A write-off removes a bad loan from the balance sheet; it does not mean the money came back. Banks may still pursue recovery on written-off loans, but a falling GNPA driven mainly by write-offs is an accounting clean-up, not a sign that borrowers are repaying.

children.text: Credit Cost: Where Asset Quality Hits Profit

Suppose a bank's average advances are ₹80,000 crore and it charges ₹1,600 crore of loan loss provisions to its P&L in a year. Its credit cost is 1,600 ÷ 80,000 = 2.0%. If its NIM is around 3.5%, a 2% credit cost eats a large part of what the lending business earned before operating expenses. Credit cost varies sharply by segment: secured home loans typically carry very low credit costs, while unsecured personal loans, credit cards, and microfinance carry much higher ones. That is the trade-off behind the high-NIM lending you met in the last lesson.

children.text: India's Bad Loan Cycle: A Decade in Brief

body.title: From Hidden Stress to Multi-Year Lows

events.title: The lending boom
events.description: Banks, especially public sector banks, lent heavily to infrastructure, power, steel, and telecom projects. Many projects stalled on clearances, fuel shortages, and slowing demand, and loans were often restructured rather than recognised as bad.

events.title: The Asset Quality Review
events.description: The RBI's Asset Quality Review pushed banks to recognise stressed loans they had been carrying as standard. Reported NPAs and provisions jumped, and several public sector banks posted large losses.

events.title: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code
events.description: The IBC created a time-bound process for resolving defaulted companies, giving lenders a stronger recovery tool.

events.title: The peak
events.description: The gross NPA ratio of India's scheduled commercial banks peaked at around 11%, with public sector banks considerably higher.

events.title: Shocks spread
events.description: The IL&FS default in 2018 triggered stress across NBFCs. In March 2020, the RBI placed Yes Bank under a moratorium and a reconstruction scheme led by SBI followed.

events.title: Clean balance sheets
events.description: With old bad loans resolved, written off, or heavily provided for, and new lending more cautious, system GNPA fell steadily to multi-year lows of around 2% to 3% by 2024 to 2025. Bank profits and public sector bank stocks rerated sharply.

body.title: PCR with and without technical write-offs

children.text: Banks often report two PCR figures. The first counts only provisions against NPAs still on the books. The second, usually higher, also counts technical write-offs: bad loans that were fully provided for and removed from the balance sheet while recovery efforts continue. The higher figure makes coverage look stronger. When comparing banks, always compare the same version, and prefer the one excluding technical write-offs for a like-for-like view of loans still on the books.

body.title: Which Is the Best Leading Indicator?
body.question: You want early warning that a bank's reported NPAs could rise over the next two to three quarters. Which disclosure is the most useful?
options: Provision Coverage Ratio including technical write-offs
Growth in the SMA-1 and SMA-2 book, along with the restructured loan book
body.explanation: SMA-1 and SMA-2 loans are already overdue and are the pipeline for future NPAs, and restructured loans carry elevated risk of slipping. GNPA reflects stress already recognised. PCR tells you about coverage of existing bad loans, not new ones. Cost-to-income is an efficiency measure.

body.title: The Improving Headline That Isn't
body.scenario: A mid-sized private bank's quarterly results headline: 'GNPA improves to 3.1% from 3.8% a year ago.' Buried in the investor presentation: fresh slippages are up 40% year on year, write-offs have doubled, the SMA-2 book has grown sharply, and PCR has fallen from 72% to 61%. The bank has also grown its unsecured personal loan book by 45% in the year.
body.prompt: Is asset quality really improving? What would you conclude and what would you ask management?
body.modelAnswer: No. The headline GNPA fall is largely cosmetic. Doubled write-offs are removing bad loans from the books faster, which lowers GNPA without money coming back. Meanwhile, the flow of new bad loans is rising sharply, the SMA-2 pipeline points to more NPAs ahead, and falling PCR means less cushion against those future losses. Rapid growth in unsecured personal loans can also hide stress temporarily, because a fast-growing book makes the NPA ratio look smaller until new loans age. Ask management: What is driving slippages, and in which segments? What share of the GNPA reduction came from write-offs versus recoveries and upgrades? What is the expected credit cost for the next year? Why has PCR fallen, and is the bank planning to rebuild it? What are delinquency trends in the unsecured book?

body.title: Fill in the Blank
body.textWithBlank: Under RBI norms, a term loan is classified as a Non-Performing Asset when payments are overdue for more than ___ days.
body.explanation: The 90-day overdue rule is the standard NPA trigger. Loans overdue for 61 to 90 days sit in the SMA-2 bucket, just before classification as an NPA.

body.title: Asset Quality Review of Any Bank in 15 Minutes
steps: Note GNPA and NNPA ratios for the last five quarters and check the direction of travel
Find the NPA movement table: slippages, recoveries, upgrades, and write-offs
Calculate the slippage ratio and check whether write-offs are doing most of the work in reducing GNPA
Check PCR, noting whether it includes technical write-offs, and compare it with peers on the same basis
Look for SMA-1 and SMA-2 disclosures and the restructured book as leading indicators
Calculate credit cost as provisions divided by average advances and compare it with NIM
Check which loan segments are growing fastest, especially unsecured retail and microfinance, where credit costs run higher

points: A loan becomes an NPA when overdue for more than 90 days; SMA-0, SMA-1, and SMA-2 track stress before that point
GNPA measures how much of the book has gone bad; NNPA measures how much remains uncovered by provisions
Provision Coverage Ratio shows how much damage the bank has already absorbed; two banks with the same GNPA can carry very different risk
Credit cost, provisions divided by average advances, is where asset quality directly hits profit and should be compared with NIM
GNPA is a stock; always check the flows: slippages, recoveries, upgrades, and write-offs
India's bad loan cycle ran from the 2008 to 2014 lending boom through the Asset Quality Review to a peak of about 11% GNPA in 2018, before falling to multi-year lows

body.text: Worked examples use illustrative figures. System-level NPA data and historical events are approximate; refer to the RBI's Financial Stability Reports and individual banks' disclosures for exact numbers. Nothing here is a recommendation to buy or sell any security.
